themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Piling Up
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked to 5 this week versus a baseline of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1900% increase (z-score: 10.97)—suggesting either a sudden influx of dumped bikes or a newly organized removal/reporting effort in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 5 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 average per week over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 10.97 indicates statistically significant spike
Streetsblog NYC reported on bike lane obstruction in Downtown Brooklyn on 2026-04-13, suggesting elevated awareness of bike infrastructure issues in the district
reporting_angles: Are bike-share systems experiencing higher abandonment rates post-winter? Interview Citi Bike operators.
Is DSNY or a community group doing a coordinated removal sweep? Check with local CB or sanitation officials for context on the spike.

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 6 this week from a baseline of 0.6 per week—an 860% spike (z-score: 6.27)—as the district reopens patios and restaurants expand sidewalk seating in spring.
evidence: 6 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 average per week over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.27 indicates statistically significant spike tied to seasonal reopening
Gothamist article from 2026-04-13 noted 'Spring may finally be here,' suggesting seasonal shift driving expansion of outdoor seating
reporting_angles: Which blocks or corridors in Fort Greene and Brooklyn Heights are seeing the most complaints? Map hot spots.
Are residents complaining about sidewalk obstruction, noise from diners, or code violations? Interview complainants and venue operators.

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, etc.) increased to 26 this week from a baseline of 13.6 per week—a 91% spike (z-score: 4.68)—indicating growing friction over congestion, double-parking, or unsafe driving in the district.
evidence: 26 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.6 average per week over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.68 indicates statistically significant spike
Streetsblog NYC's 2026-04-13 article on placard abuse and bike lane obstruction hints at broader transit enforcement concerns in Downtown Brooklyn
reporting_angles: Are specific neighborhoods (Fort Greene vs. Brooklyn Heights) or corridors seeing more complaints? Interview NYPD and TLC.
What are residents complaining about: double-parking, unsafe pickup zones, traffic congestion? Analyze 311 complaint text for common grievances.

themes_detail.label: Electrical Issues Spike Sharply
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints jumped to 6 last week from a baseline of 0.9 per week—a 586% increase (z-score: 8.55)—potentially signaling power outages, downed lines, or wiring hazards following spring storms or infrastructure strain.
evidence: 6 electrical complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.9 average per week over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.55 indicates statistically significant spike
Timing aligns with spring weather transitions that can stress aging electrical infrastructure in older Brooklyn neighborhoods
reporting_angles: Have Con Edison or emergency responders fielded multiple outage calls? Check FDNY/utility logs for coordinated incidents.
Are complaints concentrated in older buildings or specific blocks? Investigate aging electrical infrastructure in Fort Greene and Brooklyn Heights.

themes_detail.label: Police Misconduct Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Investigations and Discipline (IAD) complaints surged to 6 last week from a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 2300% spike (z-score: 13.28)—suggesting a cluster of alleged NYPD misconduct incidents, possible viral social media incident, or coordinated complaint filing.
evidence: 6 IAD complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 average per week over prior 8 weeks—largest z-score spike in dataset (13.28)
Also related: Real Time Enforcement complaints UP 1500% (14 vs. 0.9 avg, z-score: 12.46), suggesting possible enforcement sweep or contested police activity
No Reddit or news mentions yet—may be breaking story not yet covered by other outlets
reporting_angles: What specific misconduct allegations are in these complaints? FOIL the 311 complaint texts and CCRB filings.
Did a single incident (e.g., protest response, vehicle stop) trigger a wave of complaints? Interview NYPD, CCRB, and local advocates.
Is there a geographic pattern? Are complaints clustered around a precinct or specific block?
